title: Treasury Laws Amendment (2017 Measures No. 6) Bill 2017
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (2017 Measures No. 6) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would give qualifying digital currencies similar goods and services tax treatment to money and make donations to a named research charity tax deductible.
Payments using digital currency would generally be disregarded as supplies, with an exception for exchanges for money or other digital currency under the new tax rules.
Currency changes would apply from 1 July 2017, while eligible gifts to the Centre For Entrepreneurial Research and Innovation would fall within specified dates.
changes: The digital currency definition would exclude units pegged to another currency or carrying separate valuable entitlements.
The Commissioner of Taxation could determine methods for converting digital currency values into Australian dollars.
Gifts to the listed charity made after 1 January 2017 and before 31 December 2021 could qualify for deductions.
summary.affected: Businesses and other users of digital currency, the Centre For Entrepreneurial Research and Innovation and members of the public donating to it are affected.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the bill’s GST treatment of bitcoin and deductible gift recipient status for the Centre for Entrepreneurial Research and Innovation, but criticised the government for not tightening multinational tax loopholes, raising the tax transparency threshold from $100 million to $200 million, and cutting taxes for top earners while increasing taxes on middle Australia. They outlined Labor’s alternative proposals, including negative gearing reform, trust transparency, whistleblower protections, and mandatory disclosure of tax haven exposure.

speeches.speaker: Tim Watts
speeches.brief: The Treasury Laws Amendment (2017 Measures No. 6) Bill 2017 removes double taxation of digital currencies under GST by treating them like money, aligning Australia with the UK, US, and EU, and adds the Centre for Entrepreneurial Research and Innovation in Nedlands, Western Australia, to the deductible gift recipient list until 31 December 2021.
